And.name: Andromeda
And.note: A northern chain of stars remembered as a princess left on the shore, later set among the royal family of the sky.

Ant.name: Antlia
Ant.note: A faint southern group named for an 18th-century air pump, with no bright tale of its own.

Aps.name: Apus
Aps.note: A small southern bird, invented for the far southern sky when European sailors mapped those stars.

Aql.name: Aquila
Aql.note: An eagle flying along the Milky Way, led by the bright star Altair.

Aqr.name: Aquarius
Aqr.note: A large zodiac figure pouring a stream of faint stars, best followed on autumn evenings.

Ara.name: Ara
Ara.note: A compact southern altar set in a rich part of the Milky Way.

Ari.name: Aries
Ari.note: A small zodiac ram, marked mainly by a short crooked line of two or three brighter stars.

Aur.name: Auriga
Aur.note: A northern charioteer wrapped around the brilliant star Capella, high on winter evenings.

Boo.name: Boötes
Boo.note: A kite-shaped herdsman whose leading star, Arcturus, is one of the brightest in the north.

Cae.name: Caelum
Cae.note: A dim southern engraving tool, made of only a few faint stars.

Cam.name: Camelopardalis
Cam.note: A tall, dim northern giraffe filling the space between the pole and the bright winter groups.

Cap.name: Capricornus
Cap.note: A zodiac sea-goat drawn as a wide faint triangle, low in the south on autumn evenings from mid-northern places.

Car.name: Carina
Car.note: The keel of the old ship Argo, now its own southern constellation and home of Canopus.

Cas.name: Cassiopeia
Cas.note: A queen seated on a throne, seen as a W or M of bright stars opposite the pole from the Big Dipper.

Cen.name: Centaurus
Cen.note: A great southern centaur, carrying the nearest bright star system in our sky, Alpha Centauri.

Cep.name: Cepheus
Cep.note: A king drawn as a house-shaped figure beside Cassiopeia, circling the northern pole.

Cet.name: Cetus
Cet.note: A huge sea creature stretched along the equator, sent in the old story to threaten the coast.

Cha.name: Chamaeleon
Cha.note: A small, faint southern lizard near the pole, with no bright stars.

Cir.name: Circinus
Cir.note: A little southern pair of stars named for a draftsman's compass, beside Alpha Centauri.

CMa.name: Canis Major
CMa.note: The larger of Orion's two dogs, led by Sirius, the brightest star in the night sky.

CMi.name: Canis Minor
CMi.note: The smaller dog, little more than Procyon and one fainter companion.

Cnc.name: Cancer
Cnc.note: A dim zodiac crab between the twins and the lion, noted for the Beehive cluster.

Col.name: Columba
Col.note: A southern dove flying below Orion's hare, added in early modern star maps.

Com.name: Coma Berenices
Com.note: A loose spray of stars said to be a queen's cut hair, and a window onto many distant galaxies.

CrA.name: Corona Australis
CrA.note: A small curve of stars south of the archer, a crown set in the southern Milky Way.

CrB.name: Corona Borealis
CrB.note: A neat semicircle of stars between the herdsman and Hercules, like a jewelled crown.

Crt.name: Crater
Crt.note: A faint cup on the back of the water snake, south of the lion.

Cru.name: Crux
Cru.note: The smallest constellation, a compact southern cross used for generations to find the south.

Crv.name: Corvus
Crv.note: A small lopsided square, a crow pecking at the water snake's back.

CVn.name: Canes Venatici
CVn.note: Two hunting dogs beneath the handle of the Big Dipper, in a field rich with galaxies.

Cyg.name: Cygnus
Cyg.note: A swan flying along the Milky Way, its body the bright star Deneb and its wings a long cross.

Del.name: Delphinus
Del.note: A tiny diamond with a tail, a dolphin leaping beside the Milky Way.

Dor.name: Dorado
Dor.note: A southern fish whose stars lead the eye toward the Large Magellanic Cloud.

Dra.name: Draco
Dra.note: A long dragon coiled between the two bears, winding most of the way around the northern pole.

Equ.name: Equuleus
Equ.note: A very small horse's head, just a few faint stars beside Pegasus.

Eri.name: Eridanus
Eri.note: A long river of stars beginning near Orion and winding south all the way to Achernar.

For.name: Fornax
For.note: A faint southern furnace, better known today as a direction rich in distant galaxies.

Gem.name: Gemini
Gem.note: Two bright winter twins, Castor and Pollux, standing over Orion's shoulder.

Gru.name: Grus
Gru.note: A southern crane with a long neck, standing near the bright star Fomalhaut.

Her.name: Hercules
Her.note: A large northern hero kneeling upside down, outlined by a keystone of four stars.

Hor.name: Horologium
Hor.note: A faint southern clock, a thin line of dim stars east of Achernar.

Hya.name: Hydra
Hya.note: The largest constellation, a long snake stretching under the lion, the cup, and the crow.

Hyi.name: Hydrus
Hyi.note: A small southern snake near the pole, not the same creature as the great Hydra.

Ind.name: Indus
Ind.note: A southern figure of a person with arrows, drawn from faint stars near the crane.

Lac.name: Lacerta
Lac.note: A small zigzag of faint stars between the swan and Andromeda, a lizard on the Milky Way.

Leo.name: Leo
Leo.note: A zodiac lion, with a sickle of stars for the head and Regulus at the heart.

Lep.name: Lepus
Lep.note: A hare crouched under Orion's feet, as if running from the hunter.

Lib.name: Libra
Lib.note: The only zodiac figure that is an object rather than a creature, a pair of weighing scales.

LMi.name: Leo Minor
LMi.note: A small, faint lion tucked between the great lion and the bear's hind feet.

Lup.name: Lupus
Lup.note: A southern wolf beneath the centaur, cut from a bright patch of the Milky Way.

Lyn.name: Lynx
Lyn.note: A long chain of faint stars, named for the sharp eyes needed to trace it.

Lyr.name: Lyra
Lyr.note: A small harp hung in the north, marked by Vega, one of the brightest stars of summer.

Men.name: Mensa
Men.note: A far southern mountain, very faint, lying under the Large Magellanic Cloud.

Mic.name: Microscopium
Mic.note: A dim southern microscope of faint stars, south of Capricornus.

Mon.name: Monoceros
Mon.note: A faint unicorn standing in the winter Milky Way between the two dogs and Orion.

Mus.name: Musca
Mus.note: A small southern fly just south of the cross.

Nor.name: Norma
Nor.note: A faint southern carpenter's square, set in the Milky Way beside the wolf.

Oct.name: Octans
Oct.note: The constellation that holds the south celestial pole, though its stars are all faint.

Oph.name: Ophiuchus
Oph.note: A healer standing on the scorpion and holding a serpent, split into two coils on either side.

Ori.name: Orion
Ori.note: A bright hunter facing the bull, with a belt of three stars and a sword that holds a glowing cloud.

Pav.name: Pavo
Pav.note: A southern peacock, led by the bright star Peacock, near the crane.

Peg.name: Pegasus
Peg.note: A winged horse whose body is the Great Square, rising on autumn evenings.

Per.name: Perseus
Per.note: The hero who rescued Andromeda, striding along the Milky Way with the variable star Algol.
deep: NGC 869 and NGC 884, the Double Cluster

Phe.name: Phoenix
Phe.note: A southern firebird near the bright river's end, rising before the crane.

Pic.name: Pictor
Pic.note: A faint southern easel between the keel and the river.

PsA.name: Piscis Austrinus
PsA.note: A southern fish drinking the water poured by Aquarius, marked by the bright star Fomalhaut.

Psc.name: Pisces
Psc.note: Two fish tied by a long faint cord, a zodiac group spread under Andromeda and Pegasus.

Pup.name: Puppis
Pup.note: The stern of the old ship Argo, a rich southern Milky Way field east of the great dog.

Pyx.name: Pyxis
Pyx.note: A small ship's compass on the deck of Argo, made of faint stars north of the sails.

Ret.name: Reticulum
Ret.note: A small southern net, a rhombus of modest stars near the Magellanic clouds.

Scl.name: Sculptor
Scl.note: A faint southern sculptor's workshop, and a direction famous for nearby galaxies.

Sco.name: Scorpius
Sco.note: A curled scorpion in the southern Milky Way, with red Antares at its heart.

Sct.name: Scutum
Sct.note: A small shield set on a bright cloud of the Milky Way, south of the eagle.

Ser.name: Serpens
Ser.note: The serpent held by Ophiuchus, the only constellation drawn in two separated pieces.

Sex.name: Sextans
Sex.note: A faint sextant beneath the lion, with almost no stars bright enough to notice.

Sge.name: Sagitta
Sge.note: A tiny arrow flying north of the eagle, one of the smallest figures in the sky.

Sgr.name: Sagittarius
Sgr.note: An archer, or a teapot of stars, aimed at the center of the Milky Way.

Tau.name: Taurus
Tau.note: A charging bull facing Orion, with Aldebaran in its face and the Pleiades on its shoulder.

Tel.name: Telescopium
Tel.note: A faint southern telescope squeezed between the archer and the peacock.

TrA.name: Triangulum Australe
TrA.note: A bright little triangle near the southern pole, easier to see than its faint neighbors.

Tri.name: Triangulum
Tri.note: A small sharp triangle between Andromeda and Aries.

Tuc.name: Tucana
Tuc.note: A southern toucan near the Small Magellanic Cloud.

UMa.name: Ursa Major
UMa.note: The great bear, whose seven bright stars form the Big Dipper and point toward the pole.

UMi.name: Ursa Minor
UMi.note: The little bear, with the north pole star at the end of its tail.

Vel.name: Vela
Vel.note: The sails of Argo, a bright southern group between the keel and the stern.

Vir.name: Virgo
Vir.note: A large zodiac maiden, led by Spica, lying across a famous crowd of galaxies.

Vol.name: Volans
Vol.note: A small southern flying fish between the keel and the Magellanic clouds.

Vul.name: Vulpecula
Vul.note: A faint fox running along the Milky Way between the swan and the dolphin.
